name: Video Share VOD – Turnkey Video Site Builder Script
author: videowhisper

sections.description:
Build your own video sharing site with WordPress. Video Share VOD provides the foundation for a complete video destination: let contributors upload, organize videos into playlists, review submissions and give viewers a searchable, responsive place to discover and watch. Start with one creator’s video site or welcome a community of contributors.

Designed for entrepreneurs, publishers and developers, the solution connects video contribution, preparation, publishing and viewing. Use it as an independent video-sharing platform; add optional recording, ratings or MicroPayments purchases, creator subscriptions and memberships when your business needs them.

Self-hosting keeps your videos, audience data, branding, contribution policies and monetization decisions under your control. Build on your own domain rather than rely on a hosted video platform’s editorial or revenue-sharing model. There is no mandatory VideoWhisper revenue share for using this plugin; your hosting, delivery and optional payment-provider costs still apply.

Key features and benefits

  • Build a browsable video library: organize videos with playlists, categories and tags; help viewers search, filter and sort the collection.
  • Choose how videos are discovered: Styled tiles, Cards, List, Creator feed and Justified rows support different viewing styles, with optional compact layout controls.
  • Bring uploads and imports together: use frontend drag-and-drop batch uploads or import existing server files into native video posts.
  • Prepare media on your own host: configured FFmpeg processing can create playback renditions, snapshots, short previews and HLS segments. A conversion queue helps manage processing work.
  • Offer useful previews: approved posters and short hover clips let visitors explore a video before opening it. Public promotions and full-video access remain separate.
  • Control contribution and viewing: choose native upload, publication, role and playlist rules; review submissions before publication when required.
  • Connect your creator tools: optional Media Capture adds browser recording, Rate Star Review adds stars/likes, and MicroPayments adds supported content purchases and memberships.
  • Support returning viewers: a contextual video page can show creator/duration details and accessible related videos. Optional private playback memory is available through MicroPayments.

Try the interactive video-library demo | Setup documentation | WordPress.org support

Popular ways to use Video Share VOD

  • A creator’s video home: combine a searchable library with clear previews, playlists and optional individual or membership access.
  • A tutorial or resource collection: organize recordings by topic so visitors can watch on demand and find related material.
  • A contributor video community: let authorized members upload videos while staff manage review and publishing.
  • An archive of live broadcasts: connect Broadcast Live Video to bring supported channel recordings into an on-demand collection.

Publish your first collection

  1. Install the plugin and open Video Share VOD > Creator setup. Review presentation and publication choices before saving.
  2. Upload or import a small video supported by your host and selected player. Configure FFmpeg when you need generated renditions, snapshots or previews.
  3. Add a video listing and player using the provided pages/shortcodes. Choose a layout, playlists and the browsing controls to display.
  4. Review the video and test playback as an intended viewer. Test any optional restricted-access route separately before opening it to users.

Presets retain existing roles, pages, prices, access rules and provider settings. Ordinary upload/import and standalone video tools remain available.

Native video editor blocks

Insert Video sharing catalog in the WordPress editor to choose a layout, playlist, creator and browsing controls without writing a shortcode. Initial video cards render on the server; frontend filters and hover previews use the same native listing contract. Insert Video Share VOD player with an existing native video post ID to use its configured player and current access rules. The player editor preview does not play media, prepare files or add views. Open the page to test actual playback with the intended viewer account. Existing listing/player shortcodes remain supported, and VOD works without MicroPayments.

Video presentation and playback

Use native HTML5, Video.js or the WordPress player as configured. MP4 and HLS playback depend on the selected player, source codecs and delivery setup; test the actual files on the browsers and devices your site supports.

Listing controls include category, tag and title filtering; date, view and rating-related sorting; optional AJAX updates; and hover previews. Rate Star Review can supply independent stars, likes or both. The optional FansPaysite theme supports live light/dark/system presentation.

Administrators can configure video formats, conversion settings, watermark options, upload limits and review choices. Embed and playlist tools remain available under their native access rules. See the Documentation menu for shortcode and player options.

Upload, record, review and publish

The optional Media Capture plugin gives creators one upload/record/review entry. Check destination explains current native requirements before the first handoff. Creators can correct a blocked requirement and retry the retained source; uncertain earlier saves need recovery rather than another automatic creation.

New shared-workflow videos normally become review drafts. Direct publishing requires the administrator’s explicit setting, current native permission and playable media. Background preparation retains originals and reports status or retry needs. Creators and authorized staff can review private drafts without granting anyone another creator’s source ownership.

With configured private storage and local tools, generate private posters and bounded trailers, review them, then separately approve selected public copies. Approval of the full video does not automatically approve promotional assets. Previously shared public copies cannot be recalled. WordPress privacy export/erasure and optional finished-job retention cover workflow records while retaining native content, purchases and original media.

Optional access, memberships and advertising

MicroPayments can provide supported item purchases, creator subscriptions and explicitly assigned site memberships. Compatible new member content can use optional calendar or elapsed-day release rules. Native publication/password, watch/playlist and channel requirements still apply; an expired or refunded membership does not authorize playback. Unselected ordinary videos retain standalone behavior.

Configure VAST or Google IMA when advertising fits your site. Ad tags, provider eligibility and visitor privacy/consent need their own review. Other optional integrations include Broadcast Live Video for channel archives and the recorder plugins for captured posts or comments.

Hosting and protected media

Video management runs on your WordPress site. FFmpeg and appropriate codecs/resources are needed for conversion, generated snapshots, previews, watermarks and HLS segmentation. Upload size, PHP/process timeouts, storage, memory and proxy/CDN settings must suit the actual media workload.

Page or player restrictions do not protect an openly reachable original or HLS origin. Private progressive delivery needs configured storage outside public web roots and aliases, trusted local FFmpeg/FFprobe where required, and working cron for background preparation. Existing public originals are not moved or made private automatically. Private HLS/CDN delivery, migration of older sources and universal codec/device compatibility are not included. See the access and private-media FAQs before deployment.

External Service Dependencies

Video management and playback run on the site’s configured WordPress hosting. Processing features require compatible local FFmpeg configuration.

Advertising is disabled until an administrator supplies an ad tag. With Google IMA selected, the visitor’s browser loads Google’s IMA SDK from https://imasdk.googleapis.com/ and requests ads from the configured ad tag. These requests can send IP address, browser/device information, referring/page URLs, ad identifiers and playback/ad interaction events to Google and the configured advertising provider. Configure the site’s consent/privacy choices before enabling ads. Google requires the SDK to be loaded from its own domain. IMA service terms, Google privacy policy.

The VAST option contacts the administrator-configured advertising endpoint from the visitor’s browser instead of loading the IMA service. That provider’s terms, privacy policy, tracking and eligibility depend on the selected endpoint. Optional HLS/streaming servers likewise receive playback requests, IP/browser details and requested media URLs. The site operator configures these services and their policies; no provider account is created automatically by this plugin. Optional payment plugins communicate with their own selected providers under their respective documentation.

Bundled UI/player scripts and fonts load locally. Fomantic’s remote Twemoji image mappings use native Unicode glyphs instead, so selecting an emoji or flag does not request a third-party image. Native glyph appearance varies by platform. Source/build/license references are in interface/semantic/SOURCE.txt and video-js/SOURCE.txt.

Localization

This release is English-first and includes a current translation template, with no bundled translated locale catalogs. The old generic English PO/MO from 2017 are not a complete locale and are retained outside the release as development history. Existing WordPress.org/community or site-supplied language packs may still translate some messages. Video.js supplies its own player-language resources; those do not establish full plugin translation coverage. Future bundled translations may be generated and reviewed by AI agents and should be reviewed for the site’s use, especially access, billing and consent wording.

Documentation

  • Video Site Plugin Homepage
  • Installation tutorial
  • WordPress.org support

Shortcodes

  • videowhisper_videos playlist=”” perpage=”” perrow=”” – Video list.
  • videowhisper_upload playlist=”” category=”” owner=”” – Upload form.
  • videowhisper_player video=”0″ – Video player.
  • videowhisper_preview video=”0″ – Preview only.
  • videowhisper_player_html source=”” source_type=”” poster=”” width=”” height=”” – HTML file player.
  • videowhisper_embed_code source=”” source_type=”” poster=”” width=”” height=”” – Embed code HTML player.

For more details see Video Share VOD – Documentation menu after installing plugin.

Demo

sections.installation:
1. Install and activate Video Share VOD, then open Video Share VOD > Creator setup.
  2. Review your listing, upload and publishing choices. Configure local FFmpeg and suitable storage when using conversion or generated media features.
  3. Upload or import a small supported video. Use the generated pages or documented shortcodes to add listings and playback.
  4. Test as an authorized viewer and contributor. Configure optional recording, ratings or membership integrations separately, following their requirements.
sections.faq:
Can a one-time site plan include a video?

With MicroPayments 4.15.0+, an administrator can explicitly select plans in the video editor’s Site membership access box. A current source-owned plan is an alternative at the supported paid-entitlement gate. Native publication/password, watch/playlist and paid-channel checks still apply. A cancelled, refunded or expired source cannot authorize playback; independent native purchases or creator tiers remain valid under their own rules.

Keep compatible plugins active for selected rules. Retained plan rules fail closed when their membership provider cannot verify them, including public body/excerpt/REST projection. Ordinary videos with no selected plan retain standalone behavior. Review/clear new rules before downgrading both supplying plugins. Existing public originals do not become private through a plan; configured private-origin delivery retains its range and current-access checks. Approved promotional clips stay separate and originals are retained.

What happens to media workflow data in a privacy request?

Use WordPress Tools > Export Personal Data or Erase Personal Data. Exports include your site-local job and approval details without server paths, credentials, source tokens or other people’s content. Erasure minimizes redundant workflow titles/descriptions and actor references, revokes individual future-publishing approval and stops pending work. Minimal ownership/source references and necessary public-approval evidence remain. Physical originals, prepared media, native posts, prices, purchases and access grants are retained for separate native ownership and retention review.

Settings > Media workflow links to these tools and the privacy policy guide. Workflow details are kept by default. Administrators can review and enable minimization of finished-job details after 30, 90 or 365 days. Active jobs are excluded. A retained job cannot retry or recreate a publication; use its native item or retained original for further review.

What does private media hosting require?

The host must configure VIDEOWHISPER_PRIVATE_MEDIA_ROOT outside all public web roots and aliases. WebM preparation and video promotional generation require host-configured local FFmpeg and FFprobe executables. Durable jobs need WordPress cron or a hosting scheduler; the settings show an action notice when automatic WordPress cron is disabled. Server quotas, current creator permissions and native content access still apply. Existing public originals are not migrated by enabling private storage. Browser codec support varies; a native download remains available where appropriate.

How do media approval and background preparation work?

Open Settings > Media workflow to review approval modes. Existing plugin review settings remain effective until an administrator explicitly saves a shared mode. Recommended selected roles are administrators and editors. An administrator with user-management permission can approve a creator’s future publishing and revoke that approval from the user’s profile. Existing drafts are not automatically published. Native capabilities, seller/upload lists and content access rules still apply.

Private video/audio intake through the optional shared creator workspace is saved as a durable job. WordPress cron runs preparation; configure a hosting cron when automatic WordPress cron is disabled. Results and errors survive navigation. Check Preparation in the workspace, the native editor or Settings > Media workflow before retrying. Originals are retained. Interrupted native creation or public-copy approval may require manual review rather than repeated creation.

Private creator videos can prepare a JPEG poster and an optional MP4 trailer in the native video editor, or in [videowhisper_video_promotions post_id="123"]. Review the private outputs, select individual assets, and explicitly approve public use. Automatic creator publishing never automatically approves promotional assets. Anyone with an approved copy’s link can view it; previously shared or cached copies may remain available. Generated trailers are capped at 15 seconds, 8 MB, 1280 pixels and one quarter of the source duration. Zero trailer length prepares a poster only. Full-video access and retained originals remain separate.

How do I choose a fixed listing layout?

Under Listings, select the default layout and disable Frontend layout selector. Shortcodes can override layout and select_layout.

Can hover previews be used in MicroPayments catalogs?

Edit a video and use Public hover preview to approve an independent promotional MP4 attachment. The plugin publishes a separate copy of a clip up to 30 seconds, 8 MB and 1280 pixels on its longest side. Public preview copies can be viewed by anyone with their link. Disabling approval stops new catalog use; previously shared or cached bytes may remain available. Full videos and adaptive playback files cannot be selected as the independent clip. Existing VOD-generated preview clips remain supported in VOD listings.

  • Q: How much does this video plugin cost?
    A: This plugin is FREE.

  • Q: Does this video plugin work on mobiles?
    A: HTML5-compatible renditions can play in supported mobile browsers. Available codecs, upload limits and playback behavior depend on the host and device. Test the site’s actual MP4/HLS renditions and chosen player on the devices it supports.

  • Q: What does video processing require from my host?
    A: Processing needs available FFmpeg with the required input/output codecs, adequate CPU/memory, storage and execution time. HLS playback also needs correctly served playlists/segments and a compatible player. Test upload, proxy and caching limits with the actual media you intend to publish.

  • Q: What exactly is VOD?
    A: Video On Demand allow users to select and watch/listen to video or audio content when they choose to, rather than having to watch at a specific broadcast time. For more details see https://videosharevod.com/video-on-demand/ .

  • Q: How does a VOD site generate income?
    A: By selling access to individual videos, subscriptions / membership to access all or bundled content and advertising.

Which additional membership and origin checks apply?

Player, generated manifest, playlist and embed responses also check the current MicroPayments read-only entitlement helper and associated paid-channel access when enabled. Stored paid-content restrictions remain unavailable if a required entitlement provider is absent or cannot verify them. Public paid-video posters remain available as previews; unpublished videos, videos with unmet passwords and unauthorized private videos do not expose preview posters.

Application access checks do not make ordinary upload files or an external HLS origin private. Configure independent origin protection for private media, including HLS child playlists and segments. Previously delivered public URLs and bytes cannot be revoked by hiding a page or player.

MicroPayments must provide its read-only content entitlement helper for protected item purchases and creator tiers. Keep the supplying plugin active; deactivating it does not publish retained paid media. Direct myCred Sell Content restrictions stored on video posts are not supported by the media authorizer in this release and remain unavailable, including for a user with another role grant. Use MicroPayments item purchases or creator subscriptions instead; existing sale records are retained.

Paid Broadcast channel access supports the native myCred Sell Content add-on with one default point type, manual channel offers and a verified site-local log. Current timed and lifetime receipts are checked, while expired or removed receipts do not grant video access. Shared network logs, additional payment types, missing modules and unverified native contexts remain unavailable. Do not move or duplicate historical receipts between sites to bypass this requirement. These checks do not purchase, renew, issue refunds or settle payments.

Where do I report security bugs found in this plugin?

Please report security bugs found in the source code of the Video Share VOD plugin through the Patchstack Vulnerability Disclosure Program. The Patchstack team will assist you with verification, CVE assignment, and notify the developers of this plugin.

Creator upload and recording workflow

Video Share VOD remains usable on its own with existing upload, import, listings, editor and player tools. Optional Media Capture integration can send an accepted video attachment into a native VOD draft. The adapter validates current ownership, sharing/native upload/edit permission and actual video metadata, then keeps a separate provider-owned copy while retaining the original.

Open Video Share VOD > Creator setup for short review-first presentation presets, a concrete preview before saving and links to advanced native settings/integrations. Presets fill fields only. Only the displayed layout, selector and new-workflow publication choice are saved; they do not configure offers or grant capabilities.

New workflow videos default to Review draft first. Administrators may explicitly choose direct publication, but it still requires native publishing permission, the configured sharing/publishing policy and playable media. The first draft snapshots the publication choice, so selecting Direct later cannot promote old review drafts on a retry. Unsupported/processing-required media and publication refusals remain drafts with an editor link. A native editor can explicitly review/publish a review draft using normal WordPress permissions.

This integration adds no automatic price, subscription tier, purchase, balance or access grant. It does not change existing standalone upload/import publication behavior. Publicly reachable upload files still require separate origin protection if private storage is needed.

Viewing context and processing feedback

Open Video Share VOD > Viewing experience to choose the contextual video page or Classic presentation. The contextual page retains the native player, description, reviews and final access checks, adds creator and duration context, and suggests up to four currently accessible videos from the same creator. Related images use approved MicroPayments public library posters when available; original media are not used as promotional covers.

Add [videowhisper_video_status] to a page for creators to inspect their own videos. A manual Check status again reads current file presence and publication status; it does not start conversion, retry jobs or publish drafts. Files being present do not prove conversion completed. The native editor and administrator conversion review remain the recovery tools. Remote sources may require native import review. The private status response contains no paths, commands, media URLs or other creators’ records.

This is processing feedback, not a resumable upload transport or a replacement conversion worker. Captions and protected-origin delivery remain separate integration work.

Optional private playback memory

With MicroPayments’ matching reader-state integration, ordinary full HTML5 players can offer private, explicitly enabled playback memory. The current user must still pass VOD’s complete native access check. Resume requires a click, seeks without autoplay and is suppressed when source identity, duration, current access or the owning provider cannot be confirmed.

This adapter marks only the current video’s full HTML5 player. Public samples, hover clips, embeds, arbitrary embedded media and ads/Video.js timelines are not registered for automatic position tracking. A server-generated marker binds the player to the matching private controls; it is not an access grant. Position data contains an opaque identity and seconds, not a media URL or path. Native playback/access and conversion jobs are unchanged; no recording or processing starts from this integration. VOD remains standalone when MicroPayments is absent or older.

short_description: Build your own video sharing site with uploads, playlists, responsive discovery, playback and optional membership integrations.
description:
Build your own video sharing site with WordPress. Video Share VOD provides the foundation for a complete video destination: let contributors upload, organize videos into playlists, review submissions and give viewers a searchable, responsive place to discover and watch. Start with one creator’s video site or welcome a community of contributors.

Designed for entrepreneurs, publishers and developers, the solution connects video contribution, preparation, publishing and viewing. Use it as an independent video-sharing platform; add optional recording, ratings or MicroPayments purchases, creator subscriptions and memberships when your business needs them.

Self-hosting keeps your videos, audience data, branding, contribution policies and monetization decisions under your control. Build on your own domain rather than rely on a hosted video platform’s editorial or revenue-sharing model. There is no mandatory VideoWhisper revenue share for using this plugin; your hosting, delivery and optional payment-provider costs still apply.

Key features and benefits

  • Build a browsable video library: organize videos with playlists, categories and tags; help viewers search, filter and sort the collection.
  • Choose how videos are discovered: Styled tiles, Cards, List, Creator feed and Justified rows support different viewing styles, with optional compact layout controls.
  • Bring uploads and imports together: use frontend drag-and-drop batch uploads or import existing server files into native video posts.
  • Prepare media on your own host: configured FFmpeg processing can create playback renditions, snapshots, short previews and HLS segments. A conversion queue helps manage processing work.
  • Offer useful previews: approved posters and short hover clips let visitors explore a video before opening it. Public promotions and full-video access remain separate.
  • Control contribution and viewing: choose native upload, publication, role and playlist rules; review submissions before publication when required.
  • Connect your creator tools: optional Media Capture adds browser recording, Rate Star Review adds stars/likes, and MicroPayments adds supported content purchases and memberships.
  • Support returning viewers: a contextual video page can show creator/duration details and accessible related videos. Optional private playback memory is available through MicroPayments.

Try the interactive video-library demo | Setup documentation | WordPress.org support

Popular ways to use Video Share VOD

  • A creator’s video home: combine a searchable library with clear previews, playlists and optional individual or membership access.
  • A tutorial or resource collection: organize recordings by topic so visitors can watch on demand and find related material.
  • A contributor video community: let authorized members upload videos while staff manage review and publishing.
  • An archive of live broadcasts: connect Broadcast Live Video to bring supported channel recordings into an on-demand collection.

Publish your first collection

  1. Install the plugin and open Video Share VOD > Creator setup. Review presentation and publication choices before saving.
  2. Upload or import a small video supported by your host and selected player. Configure FFmpeg when you need generated renditions, snapshots or previews.
  3. Add a video listing and player using the provided pages/shortcodes. Choose a layout, playlists and the browsing controls to display.
  4. Review the video and test playback as an intended viewer. Test any optional restricted-access route separately before opening it to users.

Presets retain existing roles, pages, prices, access rules and provider settings. Ordinary upload/import and standalone video tools remain available.

Native video editor blocks

Insert Video sharing catalog in the WordPress editor to choose a layout, playlist, creator and browsing controls without writing a shortcode. Initial video cards render on the server; frontend filters and hover previews use the same native listing contract. Insert Video Share VOD player with an existing native video post ID to use its configured player and current access rules. The player editor preview does not play media, prepare files or add views. Open the page to test actual playback with the intended viewer account. Existing listing/player shortcodes remain supported, and VOD works without MicroPayments.

Video presentation and playback

Use native HTML5, Video.js or the WordPress player as configured. MP4 and HLS playback depend on the selected player, source codecs and delivery setup; test the actual files on the browsers and devices your site supports.

Listing controls include category, tag and title filtering; date, view and rating-related sorting; optional AJAX updates; and hover previews. Rate Star Review can supply independent stars, likes or both. The optional FansPaysite theme supports live light/dark/system presentation.

Administrators can configure video formats, conversion settings, watermark options, upload limits and review choices. Embed and playlist tools remain available under their native access rules. See the Documentation menu for shortcode and player options.

Upload, record, review and publish

The optional Media Capture plugin gives creators one upload/record/review entry. Check destination explains current native requirements before the first handoff. Creators can correct a blocked requirement and retry the retained source; uncertain earlier saves need recovery rather than another automatic creation.

New shared-workflow videos normally become review drafts. Direct publishing requires the administrator’s explicit setting, current native permission and playable media. Background preparation retains originals and reports status or retry needs. Creators and authorized staff can review private drafts without granting anyone another creator’s source ownership.

With configured private storage and local tools, generate private posters and bounded trailers, review them, then separately approve selected public copies. Approval of the full video does not automatically approve promotional assets. Previously shared public copies cannot be recalled. WordPress privacy export/erasure and optional finished-job retention cover workflow records while retaining native content, purchases and original media.

Optional access, memberships and advertising

MicroPayments can provide supported item purchases, creator subscriptions and explicitly assigned site memberships. Compatible new member content can use optional calendar or elapsed-day release rules. Native publication/password, watch/playlist and channel requirements still apply; an expired or refunded membership does not authorize playback. Unselected ordinary videos retain standalone behavior.

Configure VAST or Google IMA when advertising fits your site. Ad tags, provider eligibility and visitor privacy/consent need their own review. Other optional integrations include Broadcast Live Video for channel archives and the recorder plugins for captured posts or comments.

Hosting and protected media

Video management runs on your WordPress site. FFmpeg and appropriate codecs/resources are needed for conversion, generated snapshots, previews, watermarks and HLS segmentation. Upload size, PHP/process timeouts, storage, memory and proxy/CDN settings must suit the actual media workload.

Page or player restrictions do not protect an openly reachable original or HLS origin. Private progressive delivery needs configured storage outside public web roots and aliases, trusted local FFmpeg/FFprobe where required, and working cron for background preparation. Existing public originals are not moved or made private automatically. Private HLS/CDN delivery, migration of older sources and universal codec/device compatibility are not included. See the access and private-media FAQs before deployment.

External Service Dependencies

Video management and playback run on the site’s configured WordPress hosting. Processing features require compatible local FFmpeg configuration.

Advertising is disabled until an administrator supplies an ad tag. With Google IMA selected, the visitor’s browser loads Google’s IMA SDK from https://imasdk.googleapis.com/ and requests ads from the configured ad tag. These requests can send IP address, browser/device information, referring/page URLs, ad identifiers and playback/ad interaction events to Google and the configured advertising provider. Configure the site’s consent/privacy choices before enabling ads. Google requires the SDK to be loaded from its own domain. IMA service terms, Google privacy policy.

The VAST option contacts the administrator-configured advertising endpoint from the visitor’s browser instead of loading the IMA service. That provider’s terms, privacy policy, tracking and eligibility depend on the selected endpoint. Optional HLS/streaming servers likewise receive playback requests, IP/browser details and requested media URLs. The site operator configures these services and their policies; no provider account is created automatically by this plugin. Optional payment plugins communicate with their own selected providers under their respective documentation.

Bundled UI/player scripts and fonts load locally. Fomantic’s remote Twemoji image mappings use native Unicode glyphs instead, so selecting an emoji or flag does not request a third-party image. Native glyph appearance varies by platform. Source/build/license references are in interface/semantic/SOURCE.txt and video-js/SOURCE.txt.

Localization

This release is English-first and includes a current translation template, with no bundled translated locale catalogs. The old generic English PO/MO from 2017 are not a complete locale and are retained outside the release as development history. Existing WordPress.org/community or site-supplied language packs may still translate some messages. Video.js supplies its own player-language resources; those do not establish full plugin translation coverage. Future bundled translations may be generated and reviewed by AI agents and should be reviewed for the site’s use, especially access, billing and consent wording.
